title: Buying and making the slapstick
summary: He bought a slapstick after seeing one in a shop, as old-time drummers used them, and says the one Russell made of oak flooring snaps better.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: And I wanted to ask about the, I know you do play the slapstick, you know? Yeah. We all got a kick out of that. When did you start that? Well, I'm going to tell you.

You know when I bought that, you know when I got one of them? You know what I'm known is when I blee had one of them singers. I went to World Lines, I blee, and I seen one of them singers in the showcase, you know?
I said, I asked to me, I said, I said, what is that, you know?
He said, that's a slapstick. I bought it, you know? Oh, Mr. Bill, that must have been wrong when in the 30s. The old time drummers used to use them.
I know Baby Dodds in Chicago had one of them. He showed it to me years ago. Yeah.
Did you ever see drummers use them around?

Yeah, I've seen drummers use them, huh? Yes, that's right. So, I'll be just how I come to buy that thing. Somebody I seen with one like that. Yeah. And I went to the World Lines and seen it in there, you see? Yeah. So, it wasn't good as the one I make.

Oh, no, it wasn't good as that, Mr. Bill. That one you made for Charlie. Yeah, it wasn't good, you see? It wasn't made out of a kind of cheap kind of wood, you see? You make them out of good oak. Good oak, yes. A piece of flooring, wasn't it? That's the best. Yeah. You see, you get more of a, what you call it. It's a good snap to a hill. Yeah, better, yeah, you see? So, and another thing, Mr. Bill, I bought a derby. It was a luminal derby. You know what I mean? It's whatever for your trumpet, you know what I mean? I'm the first one to have one in this town.
